title: Geim, Novoselov and the Friday Night Scotch Tape Miracle
summary: During playful 'Friday Night Experiments' at the University of Manchester, two physicists used simple adhesive Scotch tape to repeatedly peel layers off graphite pencil lead until they isolated a two-dimensional sheet just one atom thick: ultra-strong, ultra-conductive graphene.
keywords: Geim, Novoselov and the Friday Night Scotch Tape Miracle
Isolation of Single-Layer Graphene via Mechanical Exfoliation
full_text:
In 2004 CE, the frontiers of human understanding were transformed through the indomitable persistence of Andre Geim & Konstantin Novoselov.

At the time, the reigning scientific establishment in the field of Nanotechnology & Two-Dimensional Materials was constrained by orthodox paradigms that could no longer account for emerging experimental anomalies. While many researchers looked past these discrepancies or dismissed them as instrument artifacts, Andre Geim & Konstantin Novoselov recognized that the anomaly was itself a beacon pointing toward an undiscovered law of nature.

Working from primary documentation recorded in *Electric Field Effect in Atomically Thin Carbon Films (Science, 2004)* (Vol. 306, Issue 5696, pp. 666–669; Nobel Prize (2010)), the breakthrough emerged through painstaking methodology. Every alternative hypothesis was systematically tested, isolated, and eliminated under rigorous controls.

During playful 'Friday Night Experiments' at the University of Manchester, two physicists used simple adhesive Scotch tape to repeatedly peel layers off graphite pencil lead until they isolated a two-dimensional sheet just one atom thick: ultra-strong, ultra-conductive graphene.

The discovery of Isolation of Single-Layer Graphene via Mechanical Exfoliation did not merely answer a localized puzzle; it triggered a profound paradigm shift across Nanotechnology & Two-Dimensional Materials. Today, its principles form the bedrock of modern empirical science, reminding every student that progress is forged when courageous curiosity meets disciplined observation.
